options.text: The gametes, such as sperm, egg, pollen and ovum

questions.stem: State the two reasons meiosis is important.
questions.modelAnswer: It produces the gametes for sexual reproduction and it increases the genetic variation of offspring.

questions.stem: Describe how the number of divisions in meiosis compares with mitosis.
questions.modelAnswer: Meiosis divides twice, so four haploid cells form, while mitosis divides once and yields two diploid cells.

questions.stem: Explain why the chromosome number must halve during gamete formation.
questions.modelAnswer: Two gametes fuse at fertilisation, so each must carry half a set; otherwise the zygote would hold double the normal chromosome number every generation.

questions.stem: A pollen grain counts 12 chromosomes and the plant's body cells count 24. Which process made the pollen grain, and how many chromosomes did its parent cell start with?
questions.modelAnswer: Meiosis made the haploid pollen grain, and its diploid parent cell started from 24 chromosomes before the halving.

questions.stem: State two differences between mitosis and meiosis.
questions.modelAnswer: Mitosis produces two genetically identical diploid cells for growth and repair, while meiosis produces four genetically different haploid gametes.

questions.stem: Name the products of each division.
questions.modelAnswer: Mitosis gives identical body cells and meiosis gives haploid gametes.

questions.stem: Explain why confusing the two divisions loses marks so readily.
questions.modelAnswer: Their outputs differ in number, ploidy and genetic identity all at once, so an answer naming the wrong division contradicts every feature the mark scheme checks.

questions.stem: A root tip grows longer and a pollen grain forms in the same plant. Match each event to its division and give one reason for each.
questions.modelAnswer: Root growth uses mitosis because new identical diploid cells extend the tissue, and pollen formation uses meiosis because gametes must be haploid and genetically different.
